Good.

### Potential bug: User percent escape `chr(int(...))` for `%00` gives NUL then rejected not in USER_CHARS. no exception.
### Potential bug: Raw user with `%ff` etc rejected.
### Potential bug: Raw user may include multiple @? host fail.

### Potential issue: URI scheme case-insens but parse_uri slices `uri[:4].lower()`; tel has length at least? if exactly `'TEL:'` len4, lowered `'tel:'`, calls _parse_tel len<5 fail. Good.
### Potential issue: `sip:` scheme followed tel etc.

### Potential issue: request line URI must be sip; our parse_uri returns kind. If string starts `SIP:` yes. If `tel:` kind tel -> syntax. 
### Potential issue: From/To PPI etc permit either scheme. yes.

### Potential issue: `sip:anonymous@anonymous.invalid` as request URI with display? no display.
### Potential issue: anonymous as To with tag. okay.
### Potential issue: anonymous in From local skip exact after normalization.
### Potential issue: anonymous in PAI syntax. yes.

### Potential issue: PAI with two addresses exactly one sip/tel, but if one scheme is `sips` parse fails. yes.
### Potential issue: PAI list repeated fields and total order. yes.

### Potential issue: Display name with `;tag` inside quotes not treated tag. Our semicolon scanner quote-aware. Good.
### Potential issue: Display name with escaped quote preceding semicolon etc. scanner.
### Potential issue: Display name quoted comma PAI splitter quote-aware.
### Potential issue: Display name quoted angle data PAI splitter angle-aware? in_quote prevents in_angle set. good.
### Potential issue: Display unquoted cannot contain angle but angle begins URI.
### Potential issue: quote in URI invalid: inner parse fails. 
### Potential issue: invalid address with quoted string inside angle? fail.

### Potential issue: Semicolon in PAI field after URI but inside `<...>`; splitter in_angle ignores, parse URI fails. correct.
### Potential issue: PAI parser treats comma in angle bracket as inside, parse fails. correct.
### Potential issue: PAI no empty list members. yes.

### Potential issue: `parse_from_or_to` top-level semicolon scanner sees semicolon **after a closing quoted display but before angle**, splits; address part quoted display without angle fails. Syntax anyway.
### Potential issue: semicolon **inside an unquoted display token** not token, syntax. scanner splits causing fail. fine.
### Potential issue: multiple semicolons one after another regex fails. correct "No other header parameters".
### Potential issue: Semicolon in tag value invalid token anyway; scanner first splits at first after URI; regex sees rest with second ; and fails.
### Potential issue: Whitespace around tag value and outside. yes.
### Potential issue: Tag value can be `tag` etc. yes.
### Potential issue: tag parameter name exactly 3 letters and case-insens. yes.
### Potential issue: Tag `;tagged=x` regex expects tag then whitespace=; sees 'g' where should [ \t]*=, fail. good.
### Potential issue: Tag `;tag==x` regex after = expects value, captures `=x`, token check rejects '='. good.
### Potential issue: tag value `%` token char accepted. yes.
### Potential issue: Tag empty but quoted value `""` token chars quote not allowed, fail. good.
### Potential issue: Tag length count token chars; regex captures no spaces; loop. good.

### Potential issue: Content-Length with Unicode digits. Global header char check rejects nonASCII before regex. yes.
### Potential issue: CSeq with nonASCII digits. reject.
### Potential issue: Call-ID underscore etc.
### Potential issue: Privacy Unicode case lower irrelevant nonASCII reject.
### Potential issue: Header names Unicode.
### Potential issue: Body nonASCII.

### Potential issue: Request line method `INVITE` CSeq method. 
### Potential issue: Request URI parse normalizes host etc. 
### Potential issue: To tel with display. 
### Potential issue: From tel selected lookup and output canonical sip.
